src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: What is the scientific name of Ashwagandha?
x: Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
x:

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Goiter is characterized by:
x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
x: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules into seeds.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: Viscosity is measured in:
x: Viscosity is measured in poise (CGS unit); the SI unit is the pascal-second (1 Pa·s = 10 poise).

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
x: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
x: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: Sun drying is a method of:
x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: In periodic table helium is placed at
x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
s: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
x: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

src: APPSC Group-II 2011
s: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
x: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2008 (20-04-2008)
s: Inflammable air is:
x: Henry Cavendish (1766) called hydrogen 'inflammable air' because it burns; the name 'hydrogen' was given later by Lavoisier.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: In Pavlovian conditioning paradigm as developed originally which of the following was used as independent variable?
x: In Pavlov's original paradigm the experimenter varied the number of pairings of the conditioned stimulus (bell) with the unconditioned stimulus (food) – the independent variable; response magnitude and latency were the measured (dependent) variables.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
x: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Which of the following is a noble gas?
x: Helium is a noble (inert) gas of Group 18; hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are reactive.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: It would be less safe to fill a gas balloon with the following gas:
x: Hydrogen is lighter than air but highly inflammable, so it is the least safe gas for a balloon; helium is inert and safe.

src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
s: 'Volume of a given mass of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature'. This statement is associated with:
x: Boyle's Law: at constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's Law relates volume and temperature.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
x: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Ignoring friction of air, if one brick and one feather are released to ground from top of a building, which one reaches ground first?
x: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g whatever their mass, so the brick and the feather reach the ground together (Galileo; shown on the Moon by Apollo 15).

src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
s: Which liquid would boil last?
x: Mercury boils at about 357°C, far above water (100°C), benzene (80°C) and ethyl alcohol (78°C), so it boils last.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
s: Which of the following is NOT an example of friction?
o: Applying brakes to stop a moving car
Revolution of the planets around the sun
x: Planets revolve round the Sun because of gravity in near-vacuum space, so there is no friction; brakes, striking a match and walking all depend on friction.

src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1995
s: A Ball thrown outside from an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth will –
o: Revolve around the Earth in the same orbit with the
x: A ball released from an orbiting satellite already has the satellite's orbital speed, so it keeps falling round the Earth in the same orbit, like the satellite itself.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s: The test in which the scorer is asked to rank samples in a decreasing or increasing order of same characteristics is:
x: In a ranking test (sensory evaluation) the judge arranges samples in increasing or decreasing order of one characteristic, such as sweetness.

x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

o: A fat and a strong acid
A fat and a strong base
x: Saponification is the hydrolysis of a fat (or oil) with a strong base such as NaOH, giving soap and glycerol. An acid-base reaction is neutralisation.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: Saurology is the
x: Saurology (herpetology of lizards) is the study of lizards.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Who among of the following is not an exponent of Humanistic Realism?
x: Humanistic realism is a 16th-century Renaissance school whose exponents were Erasmus, Rabelais and Milton; Aristotle is an ancient Greek philosopher, not one of its exponents. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Who opined, "The world is continuously evolving towards greater degree of perfection that is God." It is the opinion of
x: The idea that the world is continuously evolving towards a greater perfection that is God (the Divine) is Sri Aurobindo's theory of spiritual evolution. Aristotle (the printed key) spoke of an unmoved mover, not of the world evolving into God; Plato and Russell do not hold this view. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: New ideas (Eureka) suddenly come in the minds of the creative children in which of the following stage?
x: In Wallas's stages of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) the sudden 'Eureka' insight comes at illumination. Off-subject (educational psychology).

src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
s: Which of the following forces is responsible for all the nucleons to be concentrated in the nucleus?
x: The strong nuclear force, short-range and far stronger than electrostatic repulsion, binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Off-subject (physics).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The most malleable metal is
x: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: The magnitude of root pressure would be minimum during
x: Root pressure is lowest in summer, when heavy transpiration pulls water up and the positive root pressure largely disappears. It is highest in the rainy season, when absorption is high and transpiration low, so Rainy season was wrong.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: A metric chain of 20 metre length consists of ____ links.
x: A 20 m metric chain has 100 links of 0.2 m (20 cm) each.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud

x: Prime-rated diesel generator sets are allowed a 10% overload for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation. Off-topic (electrical engineering).

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A

x: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is
x: The exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex, always add up to 360°. Off-topic (mathematics).

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: What happens if you plug in a heater device rated for 110 V, 50 Hz in a household AC electric supply plug in India?

Its heat supply would be poorer than its rated value.
You cannot use such a device in an Indian Plug
x: On India's 230 V supply a 110 V heater draws about (230/110)² ≈ 4 times its rated power, so its element burns out quickly. Off-topic (physics).

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
x: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: In which of the following season human beings require food with more fat content
x: In winter the body needs more energy to keep warm, so fat-rich (energy-dense) food is needed most then. Off-topic (nutrition).

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
x: No standard source (ICMR-NIN RDA) gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement; deficiency signs such as night blindness peak in the hot pre-harvest season, while the printed key says winter. Left unkeyed. Off-topic (nutrition).

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene

x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is a diuretic
x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide; the iron combines with oxygen and water, so the weight increases. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2010 (25-10-2010)

x: Aluminium is keyed: light, abundant and corrosion-resistant, it is used very widely in nearly pure form (foils, cans, sheets, conductors); silver is scarce and iron is used mostly as steel. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot

x: Graphite is an inorganic layered form of carbon used as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: If a piece of wood and a piece of iron are placed in a fridge and taken out after 15 minutes, which one would feel more cold on touching?
x: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster and feels colder, though both are at the same temperature. Wood is a poor conductor.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A

x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: Skull of mammals is
x: Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional

x: Alum (potash alum) supplies Al3+ ions that neutralise the charge on suspended clay particles so they coagulate and settle. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving at a constant velocity will continue moving at a constant velocity, unless it is acted on by an unbalanced force". This law is called as ____.
x: Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The second law gives F = ma, the third deals with action and reaction, and there is no fourth law.
