x: Displacement is the shortest straight-line path between the initial and final positions; distance is the actual path length. Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
x: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so the current rises very sharply (which blows the fuse). Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: When any one experiences acidity problem, he may get immediate relief by taking a glass of water in which, a tea spoon of the following substance is dissolved?
x: Acidity is neutralised by a weak base such as baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) or an antacid dissolved in water; a strong base would harm the body.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: When a synchronous motor is running at synchronous speed, the damper winding produces
x: At synchronous speed there is no relative motion between the rotor and the rotating field, so no current is induced in the damper winding and it produces no torque.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
s:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct with respect to definition of anatomy and physiology?

I. Physiology focuses on the physical arrangement of parts in the body.

II. Anatomy studies the inner functioning of cells, tissues and organs.
o: Only statement I is not correct
Only statement II is not correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Both statements I and II are correct
x: Both statements swap the definitions: anatomy studies the structure (physical arrangement) of body parts, physiology studies how cells, tissues and organs function – so both are not correct.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: How much heat is required to increase the temperature of 1 gram kerosene by 1 degree centigrade?
x: The specific heat of kerosene is about 2.1 J/g°C, i.e. about 0.5 cal per gram per °C (water = 1 cal). A physics question, moved.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: What is the approximate value of 1 calorie in Joules?
x: 1 calorie = 4.186 J, i.e. about 4.2 J (Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat). A physics question, moved.

src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
s: Which liquid is represented by the Volume-Temperature Curve? (The curve shows volume falling from 0°C to a minimum at 4°C and rising again up to 10°C.)
x: Water contracts from 0°C to 4°C (maximum density) and expands above it – the anomalous expansion of water.

src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
s: Which of the following is a procedure used to save an abscessed tooth in which the pulp chamber is cleaned out, disinfected, and filled with a permanent filling?
x: Root canal therapy cleans, disinfects and fills the pulp chamber of an abscessed tooth; gum grafts and gingivoplasty treat gums. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as _____ to give saturated hydrocarbons.
x: Hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons uses a nickel (or Pd/Pt) catalyst. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Grass appears green because
x: Grass looks green because chlorophyll reflects green light and absorbs the rest. Off-topic (physics/biology), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: Pick up the correct pair among the following.
x: In chain surveying a ranging rod is set up to mark the position of stations and to range (align) survey lines; it does not measure distance or angles.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human female reproductive system?
x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the MALE reproductive system; fimbriae (of the fallopian tube), cervix and endometrium (uterine lining) are female parts.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Plants that complete their life cycle within one season are called
x: Plants that complete their life cycle in one season are annuals, also called seasonal plants; biennials take two seasons/years and perennials live many years.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
s: Which of the following is responsible for slowing down a moving object?
x: Friction is the force that opposes motion and slows a moving object.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the male reproductive system; ovary, uterus and fallopian tube are female organs. (Biology; moved.)

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory?
x: John Dalton put forward his atomic theory in the early 1800s and published it in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' (1808), the year usually asked.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
s: Which of the following is NOT an example of gravity?
o: Revolution of planets around the sun
A rock rolling down a hill
Formation of tides in the ocean
x: Writing with a pencil works by friction, not gravity; planetary revolution, a rock rolling downhill and tides are effects of gravity.

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: The following is generally used in bone healing in humans?
x: Cissus quadrangularis (hadjod, 'bone-setter') is the herb traditionally used for bone healing; garlic, black pepper and onion are not.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: The purpose of child lock feature in a car/vehicle is to:
o: automatic closing of the door by the driver
x: A child lock disables the inside handle of a rear door so it cannot be opened from inside; it can still be opened from outside.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I - Table-II

A. Lipase -
1. Breaks lactose

B. Amylase -
2. Breaks fat

C. Trypsin -
3. Breaks starch

D. Lactase -
4. Breaks Protein
x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: Which plants are called naked-seeded plants?
x: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines, cycas) bear naked seeds not enclosed in a fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits. (Moved to general science.)

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, so the seeds and progeny are weaker; cross-pollination gives vigour and new varieties. (Moved to general science.)

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: The synthesis of Urea occurs in:
x: Urea is made in the liver through the ornithine (urea) cycle and excreted by the kidneys.

src: APPSC Group-II 2008
s: The first synthetically prepared organic compound was
x: Friedrich Wohler synthesised urea from inorganic ammonium cyanate in 1828, the first organic compound made in a laboratory.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: A boat filled with heavy stones is in a lake. If the stones are thrown into the lake, the level of water with respect to the boat would?
x: A floating boat displaces water equal to the stones' weight; sunk, the stones displace only their volume, so the lake level falls (and the lighter boat rides higher).

src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
s: In humans, Milk Teeth generally fall off at what age?
x:
Most books and keys: between 6 and 8 years. Strictly: shedding starts at about 6 and is complete by about 12 (incisors 6-8, canines and molars 9-12) (AAP healthychildren.org; Wikipedia 'Deciduous teeth').
Milk (deciduous) teeth begin to fall at about 6 years, and the incisors are shed by about 6-8 years, so most keys give 6-8. Shedding of canines and molars continues until about 12, which is why 10-12 is only the end of the process.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: The study of grasses is known as:
x: Agrostology is the study of grasses; agronomy is crop science and anthology a collection of writings.

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: Which of the following is an example of colloid?
x: Milk is the classic colloid (an emulsion of fat in water); sugar solution is a true solution and muddy water a suspension. (Water-in-oil is also an emulsion, but milk is the textbook answer.)

src: UPSC Civil Services 2011
s:
A company marketing food products advertise that its items do not contain trans-fats. What does this campaign signify to the customers?

A. The food products are not made out of hydrogenated oils.

B. The food products are not made out of animal fats/oils.

C. The oils used are not likely to damage the cardiovascular health of the consumers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 'No trans-fats' means no partially hydrogenated oils (A) and so less harm to heart health (C); animal fats may still be used (small natural trans fats aside), so B does not follow.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The classical example for closed wound is
x: A contusion (bruise) is the classic closed wound, with the skin unbroken; lacerated, penetrating and incised wounds are open.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: The beak of an insect eating bird would be?
x: Insect-eating birds have long, sharp/pointed beaks to pick insects (woodpecker, kingfisher-type); short strong beaks crack seeds. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
s: Which is the correct statement about a genetic code?
o: UAC, UAG, and UGA are stop codons.
Initiation codon AUG codes for arginine.
x: The genetic code is a triplet (codon of three bases) and nearly universal; stop codons are UAA, UAG, UGA (not UAC); AUG codes for methionine. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
s: The strike plate of a match box is made up of
x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistant,
s: The strike plate of a match box is is made up of
x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: Which of the following is NOT the advantage of dumpy level over the wye level?
o: Simpler construction with fewer movable parts
Adjustment tested with greater rapidity and ease
x: The dumpy level's advantages are simpler construction, fewer adjustments and longer-lasting adjustments; quick and easy testing of adjustments is the advantage of the wye level.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
x: Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: What is the principle of working of transformer?
x: A transformer works on mutual induction: a changing current in the primary coil induces an emf in the secondary coil.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: The pH value of Curd as compared to that of Milk would be?
x: Curd contains lactic acid formed by bacteria from lactose, so it is more acidic than milk and its pH is lower (about 4-4.5 against 6.5-6.7).

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: In a healthy adult, what is the approximate percentage of white blood cells in total blood volume?
x: White blood cells (with platelets) form well under 1% of blood volume (the thin buffy coat), so 'one percent' is the nearest figure.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: For a transformer operating at constant load current, maximum efficiency will occur at
x: At constant load current the copper loss is fixed, so output and efficiency are highest at unity power factor. Off-topic here (electrical engineering).

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: ATP molecule releases about how much energy?
x: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP releases about 30.5 kJ/mol (7.3 kcal/mol) under standard conditions.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Normally how many number of Autosomes will be present in human beings?
x: Human cells have 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs (44) of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: In the fluorescent tube circuit the function of the choke is primarily to
at: Initiate the arc and stabilize it
x: The choke (ballast) gives a high-voltage kick to strike the arc in the tube and then limits the current to keep it stable.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
x: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the pharynx to the stomach; the duodenum and jejunum are parts of the small intestine and the pylorus is the stomach's outlet.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is used in titration
x: A burette delivers measured volumes of titrant in a titration; a pipette transfers a fixed volume.

src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
s: Which cranial nerve in humans is the largest and has both, sensory and motor functions?
x: The trigeminal (5th) nerve is the largest cranial nerve and has both sensory and motor fibres.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: The structural carbohydrates of vegetables and fruits are
x: Cellulose is the structural carbohydrate of plant cell walls in fruits and vegetables.

src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is not a solid form of medicine
x: Syrup is a liquid dosage form; tablets, capsules and boluses are solid.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Genes controlling the body characteristics are found in
x: Genes for body characters are carried by both sperms and eggs, which each pass one set of chromosomes.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: Which of the following coloured lights has the highest wavelength?
x: Red light has the longest wavelength of visible light (about 620–750 nm); yellow, green and blue are progressively shorter.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The thermite process is used to weld railway tracks; it involves a reaction between
x: The thermite reaction is between iron oxide and aluminium; aluminium reduces the oxide and the molten iron produced welds rail joints.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: Which of the following nuts has the highest potassium content per equal weight?
x: Per 100 g, almonds (about 730 mg) have more potassium than peanuts (~705 mg), cashews (~660 mg) and walnuts (~440 mg).

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What is the term for water contained within the cell wall of wood?
x: Water held within the cell walls of wood is bound (hygroscopic) water; free water fills the cell cavities. Wood-science texts call it bound water.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: What happens when a dry litmus paper is exposed to Anhydrous hydrochloric acid vapor?
o: Colour changes from blue to red
x: Dry HCl gas does not ionise without water, so dry litmus paper shows no colour change.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: The Elements of Group IA are called:
x: Group IA (Group 1) elements – lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium – are the alkali metals. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Galvanization is a method of protecting iron from corrosion by coating the iron with a thin layer of which of the following element?
x: Galvanisation coats iron with a thin layer of zinc. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
s: In Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides on treatment with-metal in dry ethereal (free from moisture) solution give higher alkanes.
x: The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether to give higher alkanes. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: In Chlorophyll, the central metal ion is?
x: Magnesium is the central metal ion of chlorophyll. Off-topic (biology).

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which metal coating is used in Galvanization process to protect Steel and Iron from rusting?
x: Galvanisation coats steel and iron with zinc to stop rusting. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Which of the following metal is the best conductor of electricity?
x: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, ahead of copper and aluminium. Off-topic (physics).

src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
s: Which of the following is a toxic material found in automotive batteries?
x: Lead in lead-acid automotive batteries is the toxic material. Off-topic (pollution / chemistry).

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: A solution reacts with crushed-egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains
x: Hydrochloric acid reacts with egg shells (calcium carbonate) to release CO2, which turns lime water milky. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following metals can be easily cut with a knife?
x: Potassium, a soft alkali metal, can be cut with a knife; lead, aluminium and selenium cannot be cut easily. Off-topic (chemistry).

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: Which of the following chromosomes is/are the sex chromosomes?
x: Humans have two sex chromosomes, X and Y (XX female, XY male); Z belongs to the ZW system of birds.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: If an object is thrown upwards, what will be its velocity, when it reaches its maximum height (neglect the air resistance)?
x: At the maximum height the vertical velocity of a body thrown upwards becomes zero (it then falls back).

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
s: The head of a matchstick is generally made of
x:
Most books and keys: phosphorus. Strictly, a safety-match head is mainly potassium chlorate with antimony trisulphide; the red phosphorus is on the striking strip (only old 'strike-anywhere' heads carried phosphorus sesquisulphide) (general knowledge, not checked).
Exam keys answer phosphorus for the match head; see the dispute for what a safety-match head is actually made of.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
x: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the alveoli, across their thin walls into the capillaries. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: In vulcanization of natural rubber, the following is used?
x: Vulcanisation heats rubber with sulphur to make it strong and elastic (Goodyear, 1839).

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which of the following seeds have wings that help in seed dispersal?
x: Drumstick (Moringa) and maple seeds are winged and dispersed by wind; Xanthium and Urena have hooks, castor and balsam burst open.

src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
s: Which of the following contains high caffeine content per equal weight?
x: By equal dry weight, tea leaves contain more caffeine (about 3-4%) than coffee beans (about 1-2%), though a brewed cup of coffee has more; chocolate has far less.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: The longest fibre on the cell body of a neuron is called:
x: The axon is the single long fibre that carries impulses away from the neuron's cell body; dendrites are short and branched.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: Which of the following substances can be used as an acid-base indicator?
x: Turmeric turns reddish-brown in bases and back to yellow in acids, so it works as a natural acid-base indicator; tamarind, sugar and salt do not change colour.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The eyes of the potato tuber are
x: The 'eyes' of a potato tuber are axillary buds (in the axils of scale leaves), proving the tuber is a stem.

src: U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2013
s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: The fibre length of cotton is 1-5 cm
Recommended dose of fertilizer (kg/ha) for Pusa
Edible part of apple is mesocarp
x: The edible part of an apple is the fleshy thalamus (receptacle), not the mesocarp, so 4 is wrong; cotton fibre of about 1-5 cm and boron as a micronutrient are correct.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2004 (10-10-2004)
s: Which dog-breed and region-of-origin pair is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Chihuahua comes from Mexico, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, not China.

src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains 2017
s: What is the immediate first aid that can be administered to a victim of burns?
o: Wetting the burnt part in cold water
Removing stuck cloth on the burnt part
x: Immediate first aid for a burn is to cool the part in cool or cold running water. Stuck cloth must not be pulled off, butter or ointment should not be applied, and water should not be poured with force.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: Which of the following materials is not commonly used as sound-proof material?
x: Rockwool, wood and (double/laminated) glass are used for sound insulation; plain iron sheets reflect and transmit sound and are not a sound-proofing material.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
s: Which of the following can be prepared using Methyl Alcohol?
x: Perspex is PMMA, whose monomer methyl methacrylate is made by esterifying methacrylic acid with methanol (methyl alcohol); neoprene comes from chloroprene and Bakelite from phenol and formaldehyde.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: What is the full form of ATP?
x: ATP is Adenosine Triphosphate: adenosine (adenine + ribose) with three phosphate groups, the cell's energy currency. 'Adenine' alone lacks the ribose, and 'protease' is an enzyme class.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: The sweetest sugar is
x: Fructose (fruit sugar, levulose) is the sweetest natural sugar, about 1.7 times as sweet as sucrose.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Honey is sweeter than cane sugar or corn syrup. Which one of the following carbon sugars is responsible for this?
x:
Levulose (option 2) is the same sugar as fructose, so both options are chemically right; keyed 'Fructose' as the standard name.
Honey is sweeter than cane sugar mainly because of fructose, the sweetest sugar. Levulose is only another name for fructose; dextrose (glucose) and sucrose are less sweet.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: What is the minimum distance required to hear an echo?
x: An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later; with sound at about 344 m/s the reflector must be at least 344 x 0.1 / 2 = 17.2 m away.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following forms of sugar is the main constituent of sugar cane juice?
x: Sugarcane juice is mainly sucrose (cane sugar), a disaccharide of glucose and fructose. Glucose, fructose and dextrose are only minor components.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
s: Stainless steel pans are sometimes provided with copper bottom because?
o: Copper is not a harmful metal
Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
Oil stains on Copper are easier to clean
x: Copper conducts heat much better than steel, so a copper bottom spreads heat quickly and evenly.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: Maximum permissible earth resistance at large power stations is
x: Large power stations need earth resistance of no more than about 0.5 ohm (major substations 1 ohm, small substations 2 ohm).

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: What is the function of "stomata" in plants?
x: Stomata are leaf pores for gas exchange (CO2 in, O2 and water vapour out); xylem transports water.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
s: Which device is used to measure current in a circuit?
x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: After eating which of the following items, a person is likely feel more thirsty?
x: Salted chips add sodium, raising the salt concentration of body fluids and triggering thirst; the other foods have little salt.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: Which type of snake bite leads to neuroparalytic symptoms?
x: Krait (and cobra) venom is neurotoxic and causes neuroparalysis; Russell's and saw-scaled viper venom is mainly haemotoxic, and pythons are non-venomous.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human respiratory system?
x: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves (nervous system); trachea, bronchi and larynx are parts of the respiratory tract.

src: TSPSC AEE 2023
s:
Read the following statements about the impact of Science and Technology on the Environment and Society:

A. Technology misuse and its wrong implementation leads to the occurrence of environmental pollution

B. Scientists have proposed technology as a medium through which the environment can be sincerely helped if directed positively
Identify the INCORRECT statement/statements
x: Both statements are true (misused technology pollutes; well-directed technology can help the environment), so neither is incorrect.

src: TSPSC Town Planning 2023
s: Which of the following statements best reflects the impact of science and technology on society?
o: Science and technology have eliminated poverty and inequality worldwide
Advances in science and technology have led to significant improvements in healthcare and increased life expectancy
Science and technology have completely eliminated the risk of natural disasters
The development of science and technology has had no impact on economic growth and productivity
x: Science and technology have improved healthcare and life expectancy; the other options are absolute claims that are false.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: How many classes of levers are there with reference to simple machines?
x: Levers are of three classes (fulcrum, load or effort in the middle). Physics of simple machines, not ICT.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: Number of Incisors, Canines, Premolars and Molars in humans is respectively
x: Human adult dentition (32 teeth) = 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, 12 molars (dental formula 2123 per half-jaw).

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
o: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
x: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Colleges Lecturers (Engineering & Non-Engi
s: Which of the following are parts of the excretory system?
x: Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron in the kidney; colon, rectum, appendix and ileum belong to the digestive system.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: Which of following is NOT a part of the human excretory system?
x: Alveoli are air sacs of the lungs (respiratory system); nephrons, Bowman's capsule and ureters belong to the excretory system.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Steridian is unit of?
x: The steradian is the SI unit of solid angle; the radian measures a plane angle.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
s: Which of the following types of matter is in ionic state?
x: Plasma is ionised gas, i.e. matter in the ionic state, as in the Sun and lightning. Solids, liquids and ordinary gases are made of neutral atoms or molecules.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: How many moles of Oxygen are required for combustion of one mole of Propane?
x: C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, so one mole of propane needs 5 moles of oxygen.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: A spectral line is emitted when an electron
o: jumps from lower orbit to higher orbit
jumps from higher orbit to lower orbit
x: A spectral (emission) line is emitted when an electron jumps from a higher orbit (energy level) to a lower one, giving out a photon. Jumping up absorbs energy.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: A salient pole synchronous motor is running at no load. Its field current is switched off. The motor will
at: Continue to run at synchronous speed
x: A salient-pole motor at no load keeps running at synchronous speed even with its field switched off, because the reluctance torque of the salient poles holds it in step.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
s: Which of the following is a voluntary muscle that you can control consciously?
x: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary; smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following inputs is required for photosynthesis to occur?
x: Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll, light, CO2 and water; oxygen and glucose are its products.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: What is the density of water?
x: Pure water has a density of about 1 g/cm3 (1,000 kg/m3), highest at 4 °C.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: Designed power factor of a DG set is generally at:
x: DG (diesel generator) sets are rated at a power factor of 0.8 lagging, so their kVA rating is 1.25 times the kW rating.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Curd should not be kept in
x: Curd is acidic and reacts with brass (copper-zinc), forming toxic salts, so it should not be kept in brass vessels; glass, steel and earthen pots are safe.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: Which of the following mechanisms help prevent cavitation in the xylem?
o: Negative pressure inside the vessels and the pores
End walls of the vessels and the pores
x: The end walls of xylem vessels and their pit pores (pit membranes) stop air bubbles spreading, preventing cavitation from blocking the whole water column.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 1994
s: The pitch of the voice of the women is in general –
o: marginally lower than that of men
much lower than that of men
the same as that of men
x: Women's vocal cords are shorter and thinner and vibrate faster, so their voice pitch (frequency) is generally higher than men's.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: The capsules that contain medicines taken by us are normally made of
x: Medicine capsule shells are normally made of gelatin (from collagen), which dissolves in the stomach.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is used to control Mange
x: Sulphur ointment (sulphur, often with lime) is the classic remedy for mange, a mite infestation of animal skin.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2000
s:
Assertion (A) : A man standing on a completely frictionless surface can propel himself by whistling.
Reason (R) : If no external force acts on a system, its momentum cannot change.
Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x:
Printed key: (b) both true, R not the explanation. Many solvers argue (a), since conservation of momentum (R) explains the recoil, and some call A practically false (general knowledge, not checked).
Both statements are true, and the printed key takes R as not the correct explanation of A. Blowing air out while whistling pushes the man the opposite way (third law), while R is the general conservation of momentum.

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: What is known as the 'energy molecule' in the living World?
x: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. TNT is an explosive, ADP is its spent form and DNA is the genetic material.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: What is range of the pH value of the human blood?
x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, pH 7.35-7.45.

src: [?] (paper header not readable)
s:
The efforts to detect the existence of Higgs boson particle have become frequent news in the recent past. What is/are the importance/importances of discovering this particle?

a. It will enable us to understand as to why elementary particles have mass

b. It will enable us in the near future to develop the technology of transferring matter from one point to another without traversing the physical space between them

c. It will enable us to create better fuels for nuclear fission
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The Higgs boson explains why elementary particles have mass (Higgs mechanism, confirmed at CERN 2012). It has nothing to do with teleporting matter or with fission fuels, so only statement a is right.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
s: Which of the following is the controlling centre of a cell?
x: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and directs its activities, so it is the control centre of the cell. Chloroplasts make food, mitochondria release energy and the nucleolus only makes ribosomes.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which organelle is called power house of the cell?
x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell: they release energy as ATP by cellular respiration.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following part of a cell is called power house of energy?
x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; the nucleus controls the cell and vacuoles store substances.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which Tissue helps in the transport of water in plants?
x: Xylem carries water and minerals from roots upward; phloem carries food.

src: Civils 2006
s:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
Inventor : Invention

A. Christopher Cockerell : Hovercraft

B. David Bushnell : Submarine

C. J.C. Perrier : Steamship
Select the correct answer by using the code given below:
x: All pairs match: Christopher Cockerell – hovercraft; David Bushnell – submarine (Turtle, 1775); J.C. Périer – steamship (1775).

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: Hyper Natrimia is excess presence in blood of?
x: Hypernatraemia means too much sodium in the blood (natrium = sodium).

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: Which of the following are the main constituents of Dettol, a commonly used antiseptic in homes?
x: Dettol's main constituents are chloroxylenol and alpha-terpineol (with pine oil); it has no iodine.

src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
s: No-load current in a transformer
at: Lags behind the voltage by about 75°
x: At no load a transformer draws mainly magnetising current, so the power factor is very low (about 0.1-0.2) and the current lags the applied voltage by roughly 75-85°. Standard objective keys give about 75°.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which cells control the opening and closing of stomata?
x: Two kidney-shaped guard cells around each stoma swell or shrink and so open or close the pore; xylem and phloem conduct water and food.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: The gap between two neurons is called a
x: The junction between two neurons is a synapse; dendrites and axons are parts of a neuron, and an impulse is the signal it carries.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: Which plant is traditionally known as an antidote for snake bites?
x: Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha) is the traditional snake-bite remedy; neem, teak and sal are not.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: An example of a phosphoenol pyruvate carboxyl kinase (PEP-CK) type of C4 photosynthesis
x: Panicum (e.g. Panicum maximum) is the classic PEP-CK type C4 plant; sugarcane and maize are NADP-ME type, Amaranthus NAD-ME type.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the plant kingdom?
x: Annelids (earthworms, leeches) are animals; algae, pteridophytes and angiosperms belong to the plant kingdom.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant through evaporation at the root surface.

II. Transpiration is the main driver of water movement in the root nodules.

III. Transpiration is caused by the evaporation of water at the leaf-atmosphere interface; it creates negative pressure (tension) at the leaf surface.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
x: Only III is correct: transpiration is evaporation at the leaf-air interface creating tension that pulls water up; it is not loss at the root surface, and it does not drive water in root nodules.

src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following plant tissues contains starch grains and is known as the starch sheath?
x: The endodermis of dicot stems stores starch grains and is called the starch sheath.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: Which element is common to all acids?
x: All acids contain hydrogen, which they release as H+ ions in water.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: What is the meaning of pH?
o: To measure the pressure of liquid
To measure the density of a solution
To measure the pressure of a blood
x: pH = 'potential of hydrogen' (power of hydrogen), a measure of hydrogen-ion concentration.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which of the following is not necessary for combustion to occur?
x: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and the ignition temperature (the fire triangle); water is not needed.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: An organic compound must contain?
x: An organic compound must contain carbon.

src: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
s: Ammonia is a compound of
o: Nitrogen and sodium hydroxide APPSC PYQS "
x: Ammonia (NH3) = one nitrogen + three hydrogen atoms.

src: State PSC
s: Which of the following elements does not contain neutrons?
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
x: Protium (ordinary hydrogen, 1H1) has no neutron; oxygen and nitrogen nuclei contain neutrons.

src: R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 2003 +1 more
s: Approximately how many different chemical elements exist on the Earth?
x: 118 elements are known and about 94 occur naturally on Earth, so 'about 100' is nearest; 200–300 elements do not exist.

src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2007
s: Which of the following is the most common element in the Universe?
x: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Universe (about 3/4 of matter); oxygen leads in the Earth's crust.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: An iron nail dipped into Copper sulphate solution turns into the following colour?
x: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate; the nail gets a reddish-brown copper coating (solution turns pale green).

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Into which colour will the yellow silver bromide turn when exposed to sunlight?
x: Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to grey silver metal (photolytic reaction).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The catalyst used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils is
x: Finely divided nickel is the catalyst for hydrogenating vegetable oils into vanaspati.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron fillings?
o: Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced
Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced
Iron salt and water are produced
x: Iron reacts with dilute HCl to give iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: How much water a dripping tap is likely to waste in a year (choose nearest figure)
x: A tap dripping once a second wastes on the order of 1,000+ litres a year, so 1,200 litres is nearest.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2004 (10-10-2004)
s: Which of the following has 1 as its atomic number?
x: Hydrogen has one proton, so its atomic number is 1; ammonia is a compound.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: The bright colour of fire crackers containing Magnesium is due to?
x: The dazzling white light of magnesium in crackers comes from burning, i.e. oxidation of magnesium to MgO. Reduction and 'explosion of metal' are wrong; 'redox' is too general.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which of the following happens during the electro refining of copper?
o: Pure copper from anode deposits at the cathode
Pure copper from anode deposits in the electrolytic solution
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the anode
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the cathode
x: In electrolytic refining the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the solution deposits at the cathode. Copper does not pass directly from anode to cathode, and nothing deposits at the anode.

src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
s: What is the primary function of calcium in plants?
x: Calcium (as calcium pectate of the middle lamella) is needed for cell wall formation and development. ATP synthesis and electron transport rely on phosphorus, iron and magnesium.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Rancidity is a/an
x: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: For the examination of skin scrapings which of the following is required
x: Skin scrapings are cleared with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH mount) so that fungal elements and mites can be seen. Heparin is an anticoagulant, and HCl and dichromate are not used for this.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
s: If mitochondria is removed from a living cell?
o: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
Cell fluid would not be transported
x: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, so removing them stops the cell's energy metabolism. Reproduction and transport would only fail as a later result.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2010 (05-09-2010)
s: The colour given by excess Lithium in Lithium Chloride solid is:
x: Excess lithium makes LiCl crystals pink. The colour comes from F-centres, electrons trapped at anion vacancies (NCERT Class XII, Solid State). Excess potassium in KCl gives violet, and excess sodium in NaCl gives yellow.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: Splitting of white light into seven colors on passing through the glass prism is called
x: Splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is dispersion, because different wavelengths refract by different amounts.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: At what time respiration takes place in plants?
o: There is no need for respiration in plants
x: Plants respire all the time, day and night; only photosynthesis needs light. So respiration is a continuous process.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: Which one of the following is an animal belonging to the Marsupial category?
x: The koala is a marsupial of Australia that carries its young in a pouch. Rabbit, porcupine and squirrel are placental mammals.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: The occurrence of differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species is called
x: Differences in characters among individuals of the same species are called variation. Inheritance is passing on traits, evolution the long-term change and adaptation a fit to the habitat.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: In which of the following species is axile placentation commonly observed?
x: Hibiscus (family Malvaceae, e.g. China rose, roselle) has axile placentation, ovules on a central axis of a multi-chambered ovary. Legumes such as Delonix show marginal placentation.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
s: Fermentation of Yeast is an example of?
x: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and CO2 without oxygen, so fermentation is anaerobic respiration.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: The limit of growth is fixed by which of the following factor?
x: The limit of growth is fixed by internal (genetic, hormonal) factors of the organism; nutrition and exercise only help reach it.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The patterns of arrangement of leaves on the stem are called
x: The arrangement of leaves on the stem is phyllotaxy. Venation is the vein pattern, aestivation the arrangement of floral parts in a bud and placentation of ovules.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
x: Insects such as the grasshopper breathe through a network of tracheae opening at spiracles; gills and lungs belong to other animals.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: What is the primary function of the human digestive system?
o: To break down food and absorb nutrients
To provide Oxygen to the body
x: The digestive system breaks food down into simple absorbable molecules and absorbs the nutrients; temperature control, blood circulation and oxygen supply belong to other systems.

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
s:
Identify the correct pairs of organic chemical reactions and their mechanisms.

1. Gatterman-Koch Reaction - The formation of cyclopropanes from alkenes using methylene carbene.

2. Friedel-Crafts Acylation Reaction - The conversion of carboxylic acids into esters using acids and alcohols.

3. Etard Reaction - The direct oxidation of an aromatic or heterocyclic bound methyl group with an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.

4. Stephen Reaction - The conversion of nitriles to aldehydes in the presence of hydrochloric acid, using tin chloride.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
x: Etard reaction oxidises an aromatic methyl group to an aldehyde with chromyl chloride, and Stephen reaction reduces nitriles to aldehydes with SnCl2/HCl, so 3 and 4 are right. Gattermann-Koch is formylation of benzene (CO + HCl), not cyclopropanation, and Friedel-Crafts acylation adds an acyl group to an aromatic ring, not esterification.

src: SSC 2018
s: Pollination by birds is called
x: Pollination by birds is ornithophily. Anemophily is by wind, entomophily by insects and autogamy is self-pollination.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
s: Which of the elements is used as fungicide?
x: Sulphur (wettable or dusting sulphur, lime-sulphur) is a widely used fungicide; calcium, phosphorus and carbon are not used as fungicides.

src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following ions is essential for the opening and closing of stomata in plants?
x: Potassium ions moving into and out of guard cells open and close the stomata. Carbon, iron and sulphur have no such role.

src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
s: Which of the following chemical compound added to bread was banned in India
x: FSSAI removed potassium bromate from the list of permitted additives in 2016 after CSE found it in bread (possible carcinogen). Gluconate, sulphate and oxalate were not the banned bread additive.

src: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2008 (20-04-2008)
s: Essential element of alkaloids is:
x: Alkaloids (nicotine, morphine, quinine, caffeine) are plant compounds containing basic nitrogen atoms, so nitrogen is the essential element.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
s: Sweating is an
o: Difficult to state, which type of process it is
x: Sweat cools the body because its evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, so sweating is an endothermic process.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Respiration is an
x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Lycopene is a pigment present in:
x: Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment of tomato (also watermelon).

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: The reaction of sodium Hydroxide with Hydrochloric acid leading to formation of salt and water is a?
x: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is a neutralisation, a double displacement reaction (ions exchange partners).

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is a/an?
x: Composting is microbial oxidation of organic matter and releases heat (compost heaps warm up), so it is exothermic.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: In the Haber's process, X moles of nitrogen react with Y moles of hydrogen to form Z moles of ammonia. What are the values of X, Y and Z?
x: Haber process: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, so X = 1, Y = 3, Z = 2.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: An electric bulb is rated 11 W. What does W signify here?
o: Amount of electricity consumed in a day
x: The watt is the unit of power, i.e. energy consumed per unit time (1 W = 1 J/s); an 11 W bulb uses 11 joules each second. It does not measure light output or daily consumption.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: In which of the following arthropods is the first pair of legs on the cranial segment modified into pincer-like forcipules?
x: Centipedes (Chilopoda) have their first pair of trunk legs modified into poison claws called forcipules. Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment and no forcipules; cicadas and wasps are insects.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: What is the primary purpose of a Wasp's sting?
o: To defend themselves or their colony
x:
Most books and keys: defence of self and colony. Strictly: in solitary wasps the sting is used mainly to paralyse prey (Britannica, "wasp").
Wasps chiefly use the sting (a modified ovipositor) to defend themselves and the colony. Solitary wasps also use it to paralyse prey, but stinging plays no part in pollination or marking territory.

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: What is the function of Xylem in a plant?
o: Transport of food from leaves to rest of the plant
Transport of water from roots to leaves
x: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Phloem carries food from the leaves to the rest of the plant, and cambium makes new wood layers.

src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are grouped under Thallophyta.
R: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara lack roots, stem, leaves, and vascular system.
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are algae, grouped under Thallophyta because the plant body is an undifferentiated thallus with no roots, stem, leaves or vascular tissue. R states that defining feature, so it correctly explains A.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots through stems to leaves. Phloem carries food; cambium and cortex do not conduct water.

src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
s: In a plant transports food from the leaves to the rest of the plant through a process known as translocation.
x: Phloem moves food (sugars) from the leaves to the rest of the plant; this is translocation. Xylem and tracheids carry water, and meristem is growing tissue.

src: APPSC AEE Screening Test 2016
s: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
o: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
x: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: Which of the below is a physical change?
x: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change: no new substance forms and evaporation recovers the salt. Burning wax or wood and curdling milk make new substances, so they are chemical changes.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Why chameleon changes its colours?
o: To tune its colour with temperature of the day
The colours automatically change on their own
x:
Most books and keys: to protect itself from predators (camouflage). Strictly: chameleons change colour mainly for social signalling and thermoregulation (Stuart-Fox & Moussalli 2008, PLoS Biology).
Most books say chameleons change colour mainly to camouflage themselves against predators. Strictly, colour change serves mainly social signalling and temperature control.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: According to Sach's, the body of the vascular plant is composed of the following three tissue systems
o: Dermal tissue system, vascular tissue system and fundamental tissue system
x: Julius Sachs grouped plant tissues into three systems: dermal (epidermal), vascular (fundamental conducting) and fundamental (ground) tissue systems. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissue types, not Sachs' tissue systems.

src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following parts of the stem consists of xylem and phloem together?
x: A vascular bundle contains xylem and phloem together. The cortex, endodermis and pith are ground-tissue regions without both conducting tissues.

src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
s: Name the non-metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature.
x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature. Mercury is liquid but a metal; silicon and lithium are solids.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
s: Which of the following is a non-metal that remains liquid at room temperature?
x: Bromine is the non-metal that is liquid at room temperature. Helium and chlorine are gases.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: If a chain is too long, the corrections to the measured distances will be ____
x: A chain that is too long measures fewer chain lengths than the true distance, so the correction is positive (added).

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following can be used as Tear Gas?
x: Tear gas CN is alpha- (omega-) chloroacetophenone, i.e. 2-chloro-1-phenylethanone. Plain acetophenone is not a lachrymator.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: What should be the size of the burner of the gas stove to save the consumption of LPG?
o: Size of the burner does not matter
x: A small burner saves LPG because its flame stays under the vessel's base. A large flame spills heat around the sides. (Off-topic: energy saving in daily life.)

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which among the following does not contain crop
x: The emu, a flightless ratite, has no crop. Turkey, duck and quail store food in a crop. (Off-topic: zoology.)

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: Which of the following is NOT an example of class Amphibia?
x: Clarias is a catfish (class Pisces), not an amphibian. Bufo (toad), Rana (frog) and Hyla (tree frog) are amphibians. (Off-topic: zoology.)

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Which among the following is actually not a tree?
x: The banana is a giant herb: its 'trunk' is a pseudostem of leaf sheaths, not wood. Neem, peepal and banyan are true trees. (Off-topic: botany.)

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
s: Which of the following seeds can benifit a patient of diabetes mellitus?
x: Fenugreek (methi) seeds are rich in soluble fibre and help lower blood sugar, so they benefit diabetics. (Biology item, moved.)

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
s:
Which of the following statements is correct about Angiosperms?

A. Seeds naked (not enclosed in ovary)

B. Xylem vessels usually absent

x: Shellac dissolves in water when borax (an alkali) is added, giving a water-based shellac varnish; spirit (alcohol) gives the ordinary spirit varnish, not a water-based one.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: Which group of elements generally form coloured compounds?
x: Transition (d-block) metals form coloured compounds because of d-d electron transitions in partly filled d orbitals; alkali-metal and non-metal compounds are mostly colourless.

x: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated (CO2-rich) blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood.

x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the body (the aorta from the left ventricle); veins return it and capillaries exchange materials.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing cast iron cookware from rusting?
x: Seasoning (coating with fat or oil and heating) forms a protective layer that keeps cast iron from rusting; soap and abrasives strip that layer.

x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

x: Viruses are acellular and have no metabolic enzymes of their own; lichens, bacteria and algae are cellular organisms with enzymes.

x: Unicellular organisms like Amoeba engulf food by phagocytosis; pinocytosis is the intake of fluid droplets.

x: Vulcanisation is heating natural rubber with sulphur, which cross-links it and makes it harder, stronger and more elastic and wear-resistant (tyres, footwear). Steel, glass and cement making do not use it.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional

x: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, rectum, anus).

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge

x: Sneezing is a reflex of the respiratory system: irritants in the nasal lining trigger a forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth. It is controlled by the medulla, but the system involved is respiratory, not immune (printed key: immune system).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The ignition temperatures of four substances P, Q, R and S are 95°C, 98°C, 105°C and 108°C, respectively. Which substance/s will catch fire when they are exposed to a temperature of 100°C?
x: A substance catches fire only when its temperature reaches its ignition temperature. At 100°C, P (95°C) and Q (98°C) are above their ignition temperatures and burn; R (105°C) and S (108°C) stay below theirs, so only P and Q catch fire.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Colleges Lecturers (Engineering & Non-Engi
s: Which of the following is NOT a region of the human stomach?
x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which blood group is known as the universal recipient?
x: Group AB is the universal recipient: its plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it can receive red cells of any ABO group. O is the universal donor (its red cells carry no A or B antigen).

src: APPSC Polytechnic Colleges (Engineering & Non-Engineering) G
s: All of the following are tests for brain, spinal cord, and nerve disorders, EXCEPT ______
x: Bronchoscopy examines the airways and lungs, not the nervous system. Myelography (spinal cord imaging), electroencephalography (EEG – brain's electrical activity) and echoencephalography (ultrasound of the brain) are nervous-system tests.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting
x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions – heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing, salivation, swallowing and vomiting. The cerebrum handles voluntary action and thought, the cerebellum balance, and the diencephalon (hypothalamus) temperature, hunger and thirst.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Which part of the brain controls the process of Breathing?
x: Breathing is controlled by the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata (with the pons). The cerebellum controls balance, the hypothalamus temperature/hunger, the cerebrum voluntary actions.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: Which of the following instruments is NOT used for setting out gradient?
x: The prismatic compass measures bearings (horizontal directions), not gradients. The clinometer measures slopes and the Ceylon ghat tracer locates points on a given gradient (hill-road surveys); the dumpy level gives levels from which gradients are set out.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The complete male flower of the following plant is transported to the female flower for pollination
x: In Vallisneria the male flowers break off and float up to the water surface, where water currents carry them to the female flowers raised on long stalks, so the whole male flower travels. In Zostera (a seagrass) only long pollen grains are released and carried under water; Nymphaea (water lily) is insect-pollinated.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: Which of the following has a open circulatory system?
x: The cockroach, an insect (arthropod), has an open circulatory system: haemolymph is pumped into open sinuses (haemocoel) and bathes the organs. Fish, snakes and earthworms have closed circulatory systems with blood kept inside vessels.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Tracheal respiration occurs in which of the following organisms?
x: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Identify the organisms that undergo cutaneous respiration.
x: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The National Tree of India is
x: India's national tree is the Indian banyan, Ficus benghalensis. Ficus religiosa is the peepal (sacred fig), Ficus elastica the rubber fig and Ficus racemosa the cluster fig (gular).

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: What is the main function of worker bees in a hive?
x: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Why are roughages important in our food?
o: They help in expel of undigested food
x: Roughage (dietary fibre) is indigestible plant carbohydrate: it gives no energy or nutrients but adds bulk and helps the body get rid of undigested food (prevents constipation). Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats, body building from proteins, and vitamins from food itself – not from roughage.
